the mesenchyme of the colon and post-umblical intestine differentiate into smooth muscle before their colonization by vagal neural crest-derived cells.
colonic and distal gut mesenchyme differentiating into smooth muscle precedes colonization by vagal neural crest-derived cells.
the differentiation of colonic mesenchyme into smooth muscle occurs before its colonization by vENCDCs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the GI tract, a topic of great importance to both developmental biology and human medicine.
the early patterning of the GI tract and its colonization by vENCDCs.
the mechanisms of SMC differentiation during GI embryonic development and the interactions between mesenchymal cells and vagal enteric neuroblasts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the differentiation of the mesenchymal cells into SMCs precedes the arrival of the vagal neural crest-derived cells to the GI tract.
the mesoderm gives first rise to the mesenchyme, and then, the mesenchyme differentiating into SMCs before its colonization by vENCDCs.
mesenchymal cells differentiate into SMCs before the colonization by vENCDCs in the anterior GI tract, while in the posterior GI tract, the differentiation into SMC occurs after vENCCDs colonization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mesenchyme differentiation precedes vENCDCs arrival in the pre-umbilicale intestine and follows it in the post-umbilicule intestine.

the mesenchyme differentiations into SMCs are initiated in a posterior to anterior fashion, and that the mesenchymal differentiation and vENCDCs’ colonization are not necessarily correlated along the GI tract.
the mesenchyme of the anterior GI tract differentiates into SMCs in a vENCDC-independent manner, while the mesenchyme in the posterior GI tract does so in a vENCCD-dependent manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the differentiation of digestive mesenchyme into SMCs is not a simple process, and the timing and pattern of SMC differentiation are different from the pattern of vENCCDs colonization along the GI tract.

the differentiation into SMC occurs in the colon before vENCDC migration, and therefore, the mesenchymal–neural interactions that regulate the differentiation into SPCs in the colon are likely to differ from those occurring in the stomach and small intestine.
colonic and distal intestinal mesenchyme differentiation is not a consequence of vENCDC migration but rather precedes it.
